'''Jeremy Levy''' (born May 18, 1965) is an American physicist who is a Distinguished Professor of Physics at the [[University of Pittsburgh]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.levylab.org/members/jeremy-levy |title=Profile, Physics and Astronomy, University of Pittsburgh |last=Levy |first=Jeremy |work=Levy Research |date=15 January 2016 |access-date=16 July 2022 |archive-date=16 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220716142754/https://www.levylab.org/members/jeremy-levy |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=August 2023}}
Levy received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree from Harvard University (1988), and his [https://sherwingroup.itst.ucsb.edu/wp-content/upload/theses/JeremyLevyJune1993.pdf Ph.D.] in physics from [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] (1993) under the supervision of Mark Sherwin. After his [[Ph.D.]], he was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of California, Santa Barbara [https://pme.uchicago.edu/group/awschalom-group#:~:text=Jeremy%20Levy,University%20of%20Pittsburgh with] [[David Awschalom]]. He started his independent academic career as an [[assistant professor]] in physics in 1996 and currently distinguished professor of physics in the department of physics and astronomy at the [[University of Pittsburgh]].  He also holds an Adjunct Faculty position in both physics and electrical and computer engineering departments at [[Carnegie Mellon University]].

=== Early acting career ===
Levy also worked as a film and television actor from age 11 to 12. He acted in NBC's ''[[Holocaust (miniseries)|Holocaust]]'', and played the role of [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077025/characters/nm0506466 Aaron Feldman]. He also had a lead role in the feature film ''[[Rich Kids (film)|Rich Kids]]'', playing the role of [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079806/characters/nm0506466 Jamie Harris]. His [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/freetools/collab-dist?source=1508872&target=189017 Erdős number is 6] and his [https://oracleofbacon.org/movielinks.php?a=Kevin%20Bacon&b=id%3a2113977&use_using=1&u0=on&use_role_types=1&rt0=on&company=&use_genres=1&g0=on&g4=on&g8=on&g12=on&g20=on&g24=on&g1=on&g5=on&g9=on&g13=on&g21=on&g25=on&g2=on&g10=on&g14=on&g18=on&g22=on&g26=on& Bacon number is 2], making his [[Erdős–Bacon number|Erdős-Bacon number]] equal to 8.

=== Other professional activities ===
Apart from his research, Levy served for a decade as founding director of the [[Pittsburgh Quantum Institute]] (PQI) from 2012-2022, whose mission is “to help unify and promote quantum science and engineering in Pittsburgh.”  PQI has over 100 Faculty members in multiple departments at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], [[Carnegie Mellon University]], and [[Duquesne University]].

== Areas of research ==
Levy's research interests center around the emerging field of oxide nanoelectronics, experimental and theoretical realizations for quantum computation, semiconductor and oxide spintronics, quantum transport and nanoscale optics, and dynamical phenomena in oxide materials and films. 
Levy’s early [[Ph.D.]] research focused on the nonlinear dynamical properties of sliding charge-density waves.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sherwingroup.itst.ucsb.edu/wp-content/upload/theses/JeremyLevyJune1993.pdf|title= Ph.D. Thesis | first=Jeremy|last=Levy}}</ref> His postdoctoral research investigated the properties of dilute magnetic semiconductor heterostructures, where he developed a low-temperature near-field scanning optical microscope and used it to investigate Mn-doped ZnSe/(Zn,Cd)Se heterostructure and superlattices as well as self-assembled quantum dots.

After moving to the [[University of Pittsburgh]], Levy began a research program centered around high-resolution imaging of the spatial and temporal dynamics of ferroelectric thin films. In 1999, Levy worked toward an experimental realization of a quantum computer based on ferroelectrically coupled Ge/Si quantum dots.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Levy |first1=Jeremy |title=Quantum information processing with ferro electrically coupled quantum dots |journal=Phys. Rev. A |year=2001 |volume=64 |issue=5 |article-number=052306 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.64.052306|arxiv=quant-ph/0101026 |bibcode=2001PhRvA..64e2306L |s2cid=119403496 }}</ref> Levy was funded through the [[QuIST|DARPA QuIST]] program that supported the [https://web.archive.org/web/20050307204634/http://cosmqc.net/ Center for Oxide-Semiconductor Materials for Quantum Computation], which Levy directed for 10 years.  During that time, Levy initiated a theoretical research effort aimed at developing various families of logical qubits based on spin pairs,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Levy J | journal=Physical Review Letters | title=Universal quantum computation with spin-1/2 pairs and Heisenberg exchange | volume=89 | issue=14 | article-number=147902 | date=30 September 2002 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.147902 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.147902| pmid=12366076 | arxiv=quant-ph/0101057 | bibcode=2002PhRvL..89n7902L | s2cid=12071720 }}</ref> spin clusters,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Meier F, Levy J, Loss D | journal=Physical Review Letters | title=Quantum computing with spin cluster qubits | volume=90 | issue=4 | article-number=047901 | date=27 January 2003 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/Physrevlett.90.047901 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/Physrevlett.90.047901| pmid=12570460 | arxiv=cond-mat/0206310 | bibcode=2003PhRvL..90d7901M | s2cid=39266605 }}</ref> cluster-state qubits,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Weinstein YS, Hellberg CS, Levy J | journal=Physical Review A | title=Quantum-dot cluster-state computing with encoded qubits | volume=72 | issue=2 | article-number=020304 | date=30 August 2005 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/Physreva.72.020304 | issn=1050-2947 | doi=10.1103/Physreva.72.020304| arxiv=quant-ph/0506032 | bibcode=2005PhRvA..72b0304W | s2cid=34813592 }}</ref> and dimerized spin chains.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Srinivasa V, Levy J, Hellberg CS | journal=Physical Review B | title=Flying spin qubits: A method for encoding and transporting qubits within a dimerized Heisenberg spin-1/2 chain | volume=76 | issue=9 | article-number=094411 | date=21 September 2007 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1103/Physrevb.76.094411 | issn=1098-0121 | doi=10.1103/Physrevb.76.094411| bibcode=2007PhRvB..76i4411S | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2006, Levy visited the group of [[Jochen Mannhart]] who had discovered a sharp insulator-to-metal transition in oxide heterostructure composed of a thin layer of LaAlO<sub>3</sub> grown on TiO<sub>2</sub>-terminated SrTiO<sub>3</sub>.  The 3-unit-cell LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> was metastable and could be switched with a voltage applied to the back of the SrTiO<sub>3</sub>substrate.  Levy and his student [https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Cheng-Cen Cheng Cen] showed that a biased conductive atomic force microscope tip could locally switch the interface of the 3-unit-cell LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> heterostructure system,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Levy |first1=Jeremy |title=Nanoscale control of an interfacial metal-insulator transition at room temperature |journal=Nature Materials |year=2008 |volume=7 |issue=4 |pages=298–302 |doi=10.1038/nmat2136|pmid=18311143 |bibcode=2008NatMa...7..298C |url=https://opus.bibliothek.uni-augsburg.de/opus4/frontdoor/index/index/docId/61913 }}</ref> thus launching a new field that Levy refers to as “[https://www.pqi.org/events/correlated-nanoelectronics Correlated Nanoelectronics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308070813/https://www.pqi.org/events/correlated-nanoelectronics |date=2022-03-08 }}”.

=== Other areas of research ===
Levy has conducted research in a variety of areas:
* Apertureless near-field scanning optical microscopy, applied principally to polar nanodomains in ferroelectric thin films.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Ma HZ, Levy J | journal=Nano Letters | title=GHz apertureless near-field scanning optical microscopy of ferroelectric nanodomain dynamics | volume=6 | issue=3 | pages=341–344 | date=17 January 2006 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1021/Nl052415u | issn=1530-6984 | doi=10.1021/Nl052415u| pmid=16522019 | bibcode=2006NanoL...6..341M | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Development of g-tensor modulation resonance as a method for all-electrical control of spin in semiconductor heterostructure.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Kato Y, Myers RC, Driscoll DC, Gossard AC, Levy J, Awschalom DD | journal=Science | title=Gigahertz electron spin manipulation using voltage-controlled g-tensor modulation | volume=299 | issue=5610 | pages=1201–1204 | date=21 February 2003 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.1080880 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.1080880| pmid=12543982 | bibcode=2003Sci...299.1201K | s2cid=29734280 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Development of conductive-AFM lithography for extreme nanoscale control of the metal-insulator transition in LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3 </sub>heterostructure.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Cen C, Thiel S, Mannhart J, Levy J | journal=Science | title=Oxide nanoelectronics on demand | volume=323 | issue=5917 | pages=1026–1030 | date=20 February 2009 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.1168294 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.1168294| pmid=19229030 | bibcode=2009Sci...323.1026C | s2cid=32623248 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Discovery of room-temperature electronically controlled ferromagnetism in LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> heterostructure.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Bi F, Huang M, Ryu S, Lee H, Bark CW, Eom CB, Irvin P, Levy J | journal=Nature Communications | title=Room-temperature electronically-controlled ferromagnetism at the LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> interface | volume=5 | article-number=5019 | date=25 September 2014 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/ncomms6019 | issn=2041-1723 | doi=10.1038/ncomms6019 | doi-access=free| pmid=25254952 | arxiv=1307.5557 | bibcode=2014NatCo...5.5019B | s2cid=205330460 }}</ref>
* Development of sketched LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> single-electron transistors,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Cheng G, Siles PF, Bi F, Cen C, Bogorin DF, Bark CW, Folkman CM, Park JW, Eom CB, Medeiros-Ribeiro G, Levy J | journal=Nature Nanotechnology | title=Sketched oxide single-electron transistor | volume=6 | issue=6 | pages=343–347 | date=17 April 2011 | url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2011.56 | issn=1748-3387 | doi=10.1038/nnano.2011.56| pmid=21499252 | bibcode=2011NatNa...6..343C | url-access=subscription }}</ref> electron waveguides,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Cheng GL, Tomczyk M, Tacla AB, Lee H, Lu SC, Veazey JP, Huang MC, Irvin P, Ryu S, Eom CB, Daley A, Pekker D, Levy J | journal=Physical Review X | title=Tunable Electron-Electron Interactions in LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> Nanostructures | volume=6 | issue=4 | date= 2016 | article-number=041042 | issn=2160-3308 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.6.041042| bibcode=2016PhRvX...6d1042C | s2cid=19807411 | doi-access=free | arxiv=1602.06029 }}</ref> and other [[mesoscopic physics]] devices
* Discovery of electron pairing without superconductivity in sketched LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> devices.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Cheng G, Tomczyk M, Lu S, Veazey JP, Huang M, Irvin P, Ryu S, Lee H, Eom CB, Hellberg CS, Levy J | journal=Nature | title=Electron pairing without superconductivity | volume=521 | issue=7551 | pages=196–199 | date=14 May 2015 | url=http://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v521/n7551/full/nature14398.html | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature14398| pmid=25971511 | bibcode=2015Natur.521..196C | s2cid=4460979 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Development of 100 THz-bandwidth generation and detection of THz emission in nanoscale LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> junctions<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=Chen L, Sutton E, Lee H, Lee JW, Li J, Eom CB, Irvin P, Levy J | journal=Light: Science & Applications | title=Over 100-THz bandwidth selective difference frequency generation at LaAlO<sub>3</sub>/SrTiO<sub>3</sub> nanojunctions | volume=8 | issue=1 | article-number=24 | date=27 February 2019 | url=https://doi.org/10.1038/s41377-019-0135-0 | issn=2047-7538 | doi=10.1038/s41377-019-0135-0 | doi-access=free| pmid=30820320 | pmc=6393436 | bibcode=2019LSA.....8...24C }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Levy was born in [[New York City]]. In 1990, he married [[Chandralekha Singh]] who is also a physicist and currently a distinguished professor in the department of physics and astronomy at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. They were classmates in the [[Ph.D.]] program at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. They have two sons [https://www.akashlevy.com/ Akash Levy] and [https://ishanina.github.io/ Ishan Levy].{{citation needed|date=August 2023}}
